question: Why did water-accessible pores make up most of the total pore space of the shales after solvent extraction in the CV-SANS results?
expect: premise false: water-accessible pore space rose only slightly and still made up less than 30% of the total pores (abstract; sec. 3)
rendered:
Document: "Sequential Solvent Extraction Reveals Lithofacies-Dependent Pore Accessibility, Wettability, and Hydrocarbon Partitioning in Organic-Rich Lacustrine Shales"

The CV-SANS results show that after solvent extraction, water-accessible pore space increased in the X1, Y1, and Y2 samples. However, the water-accessible pores still account for less than 30% of the total pores in the X1 and Y2 samples. In the Y1 sample, the water-accessible pores increase from 14.4% to 17.2% on the first day of solvent extraction and remain at 17.5% at D200-ASE. 

This indicates that water-accessible pores do not make up most of the total pore space of the shales after solvent extraction.
